title: Con Law II
description: Constitutional Law II: the First Amendment, Weeks 1–15 (Chapters 1–13). Covers the Religion Clauses, the speech framework, incitement and national security, true threats and speech integral to crime, immoral speech, torts involving speech, commercial speech, content-neutral rules and expressive conduct, government speech, funding and forum doctrine, government employees and public schools, and social media and elections.

First_Amendment_Outline.html.title: First Amendment Outline
First_Amendment_Outline.html.description: Case-by-case outline of Weeks 1–15 (Chapters 1–13), from Barnette and Kennedy v. Bremerton through Counterman, Ferber, New York Times v. Sullivan, Central Hudson, Texas v. Johnson, Shurtleff, Rosenberger, Tinker, NetChoice, and Citizens United. Each case has its rule, facts, holding, and dissent. Includes checklists for each doctrine, synthesis tables, and the stretch exercises. Every case box opens in the Look up panel on the practice pages.

First_Amendment_Outline_Ch1-13.pdf.title: First Amendment Outline (PDF)
First_Amendment_Outline_Ch1-13.pdf.description: The same Weeks 1–15 outline (Chapters 1–13) as a 74-page PDF to download or print.

First_Amendment_Concepts_Test.html.title: First Amendment Concepts Test
First_Amendment_Concepts_Test.html.description: 110 concept questions on the whole course, Weeks 1–15 (Chapters 1–13), in outline order: the Religion Clauses, the speech framework and unprotected categories, immoral speech, defamation and IIED, commercial speech, time, place, and manner rules and expressive conduct, government speech, funding and forum doctrine, employee and student speech, and social media and elections. It works like Shuffle mode: shuffled choices, cross-outs, an explanation for every choice, the rule, Retry missed, and a link to the outline section to review. Filter by chapter or shuffle the whole set.

First_Amendment_Flowcharts.html.title: First Amendment Flowcharts
First_Amendment_Flowcharts.html.description: Interactive decision charts for Chapters 1–6. A big-picture map shows how the Religion Clauses and the speech doctrines fit together, and eight charts walk through coercion, Free Exercise, the Establishment Clause and funding, the speech framework, incitement and fighting words, prior restraints, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech. Tap any box for a plain-English explanation, the cases behind it, and what to watch out for.

First_Amendment_Case_Flash_Cards.html.title: First Amendment Case Flash Cards
First_Amendment_Case_Flash_Cards.html.description: 34 flashcards, one for each main case in Chapters 1–6, from Whitney and Barnette through Paxton and Brown. Each card asks what the case held, then gives the rule, the vote, and the key reasoning. Cited cases such as Gobitis, Yoder, Zelman, and Chaplinsky appear on the card for the case that cites them. Flip each card, then mark it Got it or Revisit.

First_Amendment_Concept_Flash_Cards.html.title: First Amendment Concept Flash Cards
First_Amendment_Concept_Flash_Cards.html.description: 32 flashcards on the core concepts of Chapters 1–6. Covers the Free Exercise and speech checklists, the ways a law fails neutrality, Establishment Clause funding, RFRA, the unprotected categories, overbreadth and vagueness, prior restraints, mens rea, the Miller test, and protecting kids versus adults.

First_Amendment_Essay_Questions.html.title: First Amendment Essay Questions
First_Amendment_Essay_Questions.html.description: 15 bar-style essay questions covering every case and concept in Chapters 1–6, organized by topic. Each essay sets out new facts with several questions, from a compelled state creed and a noise ordinance aimed at a night ceremony to a leaked convoy memo, threatening messages, and an AI companion app. Open the model answer for a full-credit response worked issue by issue, the cases it uses and why, the key concepts explained, and a 10-point scoring guide. Includes a case index and a coverage map of all 113 outline items.
